These interlocutory applications have been filed by the appellants praying therein to suspend the sentence and release them on bail during the pendency of these appeals.

2. The appellants have been convicted in connection with Special POCSO Case No. 52 of 2020, for the offence under Section(s) 366 and 376-D r/w 109 of the Indian Penal Code and Section(s) 6 r/w Sections 5(g) and 17 of the POCSO Act.
They have been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for twenty years and fine of Rs.5,000/- each for the offence under Sections 6 of the POCSO Act and other sentences for the other offences.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants and learned A.P.Ps and have gone through the impugned judgment, the evidence and the Trial Court Records.
4.
Opportunity was given to the State to oppose the bail, which the State availed and opposed.

sentences.text: While deposing in Court, the victim girl alleges that she was raped but surprisingly, in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C, she has not alleged the commission of rape, rather in paragraph 9 of the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C she categorically stated that nothing wrong was committed upon her.
6. Considering the aforesaid facts, we are inclined to allow these interlocutory applications.

Accordingly, upon suspending the sentence, the appellants, named above, are directed to be released on bail, during the pendency of this appeal, on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (ten thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Special Judge POCSO, Act, Dhanbad, in connection with Spl. (POCSO) Case No. 52 of 2020, with a condition that the appellants shall appear and mark their attendance before the Registrar, Civil Court, Dhanbad, once in every four months till the disposal of these appeals.
7. These interlocutory applications stand allowed.

(ANANDA SEN, J.) (GAUTAM KUMAR CHOUDHARY, J.) Anu/-Cp3 Sunny Mandal vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54214281/
